entries.why_wrong: This line only declares the function's name and parameter, with no error handling involved, so it can't be where a silent-catch bug lives.
This just declares the `config` variable with no value assigned yet; the bug is about how a later error is handled, not about this declaration.
This line only opens the `try` block that wraps the risky `JSON.parse` call; opening a protected block isn't itself a mistake, so the bug isn't here.

Tapping here treats the parse call as the culprit, but `JSON.parse` throwing on bad input is expected, correct behavior. The real problem is what happens immediately after it throws — the catch block swallows that error instead of doing anything with it.
This is just the closing brace of the catch block; the bug is that everything between the opening and closing braces is empty, not the brace itself.

This is where the confusing `TypeError` actually fires, so it looks like the fault, but `config` is only `undefined` here because an earlier parse failure was already swallowed silently. The bug is upstream, in the handler that let a real error disappear without a trace.
This line simply closes the function body and has no role in how the JSON parsing error is caught or reported above.
